newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to finance loss-making firms through loans.
newsitem.headline: Spain to finance loss-making firms through loans.

text.p: The government will use loans to finance loss-making public companies for which it is setting aside 230 billion pesetas, Pedro Ferreras, chairman of the state industrial holding company SEPI, said on Wednesday.
"In the budget it is now registered as a loan from SEPI to the Agencia Industrial de Estado (AIE)," Ferreras told reporters.
SEPI currently groups profit-making state firms while those which are losing money belong to the AIE.

Ferreras's comments contrasted with previous remarks made by Budget Office Director Jose Barea, who said the 230 billion would be raised via the sale to SEPI by the AIE of steel company Corporacion Siderurgica Integral (CSI).
"We are not currently in any negotiation to buy it (CSI), nor for the AIE to sell it to us," said Ferreras.

He added that SEPI was forecast to make a net group profit of 240 billion pesetas in 1996 and 407 billion pesetas in 1997. This profit rise included budgeted income from privatisations of 460 billion pesetas.

SEPI's total resources for 1997 will be 628 billion, which included the privatisation income, 90 billion pesetas from dividend income, tax payments and financial results and 78 billion from its own treasury.
Ferreras said he hoped to reduce the historical debt of the now defunct Instituto Nacional de Industria (INI) to 173.3 billion at the end of 1997 from 431.9 billion on September 30 this year.
He hoped to cancel the amortisation of this debt volume within two or three years.
